1.name: J.T. Rhoads
1.headline: A franchise-caliber passing foundation
1.bio: A former five-star recruit and projected first overall pick, Rhoads is a franchise quarterback prospect who excels on quick throws and deep passes, particularly when moving outside the pocket. The next level will test his timing, decision-making and ability to execute through changing defensive looks.
1.watch: Keep his base settled against interior pressure and maintain timing when the first window closes.

2.name: Jaquon Hall
2.headline: A quarterback who changes the math for a defense
2.bio: A former four-star recruit and late bloomer, Hall surged as a passer late in the season after providing consistent production as a runner throughout the year. How he responds to tighter windows and disguised coverage will shape his path at the next level.
2.watch: Stay ahead of pressure with the ball, preserve throwing rhythm and reduce unnecessary hits.

3.headline: An early pick who can change the front
3.bio: Williams is a generational edge prospect with dominant power and the athletic traits to threaten tackles with speed as well, giving offenses two elite problems to solve. Turning his strengths into a dependable role against stronger competition will be the next challenge.
3.watch: Develop quicker counters against extra protection and maintain rush-lane control when the first collision wins.
3.name: Cardarion Williams

4.name: Kenneth Bell
4.headline: An outside corner with first-round coverage upside
4.bio: Bell is the fastest player in the class regardless of position, pairing exceptional recovery speed with elite coverage ability that makes him exceptionally difficult to beat deep. His transition will depend on sustaining that profile against more polished routes and faster offensive concepts.
4.watch: Stay patient against double moves and finish consistently in run support.

5.name: Malachi Robinson
5.headline: A versatile safety with range and a physical edge
5.bio: A former five-star recruit and the crown jewel of the class, Robinson combines elite coverage, heavy hitting and slot versatility as a movable piece across the defense. The next level will test his consistency as offenses create more difficult matchups and coverage decisions.
5.watch: Pair decisive run support with disciplined angles and reliable deep coverage.

6.name: Aaron Archuelta
6.headline: An early pick with a legitimate vertical ceiling
6.bio: Archuelta combines franchise quarterback size, a rocket arm and good mobility, but an uneven body of tape leaves evaluators weighing his high-end traits against his consistency. How he responds to tighter windows and disguised coverage will shape his path at the next level.
6.watch: Layer intermediate throws, vary ball speed and take the underneath answer when the deep window disappears.

7.name: Kevin Alexander Jr
7.headline: A rangy coverage linebacker with early starting potential
7.bio: A former safety, Alexander combines elite coverage ability with the size and speed to match running backs and tight ends across a variety of assignments. More complex offensive looks will test how consistently he can execute his responsibilities at the next level.
7.watch: Maintain coverage discipline against play action and take cleaner angles through traffic.

8.headline: Size and finish worthy of an early pick
8.bio: A Hawaii native and the anchor of Ohio State’s offensive line, Pukahi is widely projected inside the top ten after establishing himself as a dependable foundation up front. His projection will depend on sustaining that approach against the speed and physicality of professional defensive fronts.
8.watch: Stay balanced against inside counters and keep his recovery steps compact when the first punch misses.
8.name: Nakana'ela Pukahi

9.headline: A heavy edge with first-round disruption
9.bio: Patrick is a big-bodied defensive end who consistently protects the edge against the run while offering enough pass-rush ability to challenge blockers on passing downs. The next level will test how consistently his strengths hold up against professional offensive linemen.
9.watch: Keep his pad level controlled and sustain his rush when a blocker survives the first contact.
9.name: Braeden Patrick

10.headline: A clean pocket starts with his side of the line
10.bio: Regarded as the best pass blocker in the class, Fitzwilliam projects as a long-term offensive line anchor with the potential to protect the quarterback for years. The move up will demand reliable execution against defenders who can win in a variety of ways.
10.watch: Create more displacement in the run game while preserving his patience and balance in protection.
10.name: Garrison Fitzwilliam

11.name: Narquise Jones
11.headline: A first-round receiver who can tilt the coverage
11.bio: Jones is a speedster whose long speed threatens defenses vertically, with the open-field ability to force missed tackles and turn catches into explosive gains. At the next level, he will need to maintain his effectiveness against increasingly disciplined defensive backs.
11.watch: Defeat patient press coverage and preserve route timing when the release gets crowded.

12.name: Willie Mason Jr
12.headline: An athletic second-level defender who can match in space
12.bio: A former five-star recruit, Mason is a rangy coverage linebacker with the speed and tools to create difficult matchups for backs and tight ends. His transition will depend on sustaining that profile against more polished routes and faster offensive concepts.
12.watch: Improve block separation and keep run fits consistent without losing coverage range.

13.headline: A first-round matchup problem through the middle
13.bio: Zakrzewski pairs outstanding production with contributions throughout the offense, offering a complete tight end profile that extends beyond any single assignment or role. The next step is carrying that skill set into a consistent role against faster, more physical competition.
13.watch: Improve hand placement and sustain leverage as an inline run blocker without losing his receiving flexibility.
13.name: Aleks Zakrzewski

14.name: Nick Gardiner
14.headline: A polished distributor with a starter's pathway
14.bio: Gardiner is a cerebral quarterback with underrated rushing ability who consistently reaches all three levels of the field despite possessing an average arm. How he responds to tighter windows and disguised coverage will shape his path at the next level.
14.watch: Maintain accuracy on a disrupted platform and create practical answers outside the initial structure.

15.headline: A first-round answer for a pass-heavy offense
15.bio: Martens is an accomplished right tackle with a high floor, a more modest ceiling and enough versatility to receive consideration on the left side in the NFL. His ability to handle different defensive fronts will shape his opportunities at the next level.
15.watch: Improve pad level and sustain his run blocks through the finish without losing protection discipline.
15.name: J.C. Martens

16.name: Mwenye Obasanjo
16.headline: A competitive outside corner with starting potential
16.bio: Obasanjo is a strong, compact defensive back who tackles well and offers the coverage versatility to match both wide receivers and running backs. His transition will depend on sustaining that profile against more polished routes and faster offensive concepts.
16.watch: Keep his footwork controlled against releases and transitions at the top of routes.

17.name: Nick Monk
17.headline: Get him the ball and let the yards follow
17.bio: Monk is a true playmaker whose ability after the catch stands out, giving his offense a chance to create explosive gains from routine touches. His development will be measured by how consistently his strengths translate against faster, more physical coverage.
17.watch: Strengthen catch-point consistency through contact and develop more outside-release counters.

18.name: Francis Smith
18.headline: An early-down engine with first-round substance
18.bio: A former five-star recruit, Smith runs with impressive balance and power, staying on his feet through contact and giving defenders a difficult assignment in the open field. His professional role will grow with dependable execution and the ability to contribute in different situations.
18.watch: Sharpen protection assignments and stay patient when the first interior lane is crowded.

19.headline: A strong edge for an offense that wants to run
19.bio: A former five-star recruit, Ellis brings a run-blocking foundation at right tackle, but must play with better leverage to make his power more consistent. His ability to handle different defensive fronts will shape his opportunities at the next level.
19.watch: Keep his feet active after contact and improve the timing of his hands against changing rush angles.
19.name: Cody Ellis

20.headline: A young tackle with real movement at the line
20.bio: Falana has played football for only two years, earning a starting role in his second season before emerging as one of the nation’s best right tackles. His projection will depend on sustaining that approach against the speed and physicality of professional defensive fronts.
20.watch: Refine set depth and recover with his feet instead of reaching when the edge gets threatened.
20.name: Salene Falana

21.name: Chandu Chukwumerejie
21.headline: A sturdy target with first-round offensive utility
21.bio: Chukwumerejie draws Deebo Samuel comparisons as a powerful receiver whose physical approach translates to the run game as well as his work catching passes. His development will be measured by how consistently his strengths translate against faster, more physical coverage.
21.watch: Add deception to route stems and create cleaner separation before contact becomes necessary.

22.name: Keanu Jones
22.headline: A deep safety who can cover ground
22.bio: Jones is one half of Ohio State’s elite safety tandem, a smaller defensive back who continues the program’s tradition of productive, high-level secondary play. His ability to handle varied assignments against faster offenses will shape his path to playing time.
22.watch: Take efficient angles from depth and secure tackles in the open field.

23.name: A.J. Simms
23.headline: A coverage prospect with a chance to compete early
23.bio: At 5-foot-9, Simms is undersized but uses his athletic ability to compensate, and his consistent play made him one of college football’s best corners this season. More complex offensive looks will test how consistently he can execute his responsibilities at the next level.
23.watch: Improve tackling and avoid guessing when receivers change pace.

24.name: Jaylan Matthews Jr.
24.headline: A first-round creator who can manufacture extra yards
24.bio: A top-ten recruit who started at Maryland, Matthews brings a highly regarded background and the experience of earning an early starting opportunity. His transition will hinge on creating efficient gains and contributing consistently across different offensive situations.
24.watch: Trust the first useful lane and improve consistency picking up pressure from the edge.

25.headline: A young edge with a clear path to passing-down impact
25.bio: A former five-star recruit, White made the most of a limited role with strong production and athletic traits that suggest room for a larger workload. The next level will test how consistently his strengths hold up against professional offensive linemen.
25.watch: Improve his contact balance against the run and connect his initial rush to a reliable counter.
25.name: Keshawn White

26.headline: A passing-game weapon worth moving around
26.bio: James is a fast tight end with rare speed for the position, giving him the upside to stretch coverage and develop into a dangerous receiving option. How reliably he handles varied assignments will determine the size of his role at the next level.
26.watch: Build a more dependable blocking base and preserve route timing when defenders disrupt his release.
26.name: Nasir James Jr.

27.headline: A first-round edge with pressure and run-game utility
27.bio: Robinson has the size and frame to dominate as a defensive end, but needs more consistent execution to turn those physical tools into reliable production. Turning his strengths into a dependable role against stronger competition will be the next challenge.
27.watch: Vary his hand sequencing and respond sooner when the blocker sits on his first approach.
27.name: Deacon Robinson

28.headline: An imposing tackle with a starting pathway to refine
28.bio: Howard is a rising prospect with athletic ability and power as a blocker, giving evaluators an intriguing combination of movement skills and strength at tackle. His projection will depend on sustaining that approach against the speed and physicality of professional defensive fronts.
28.watch: Keep his pad level controlled and avoid opening his hips before the rusher commits.
28.name: Jamarcus Howard

29.name: Cyrus Johnson III
29.headline: A long-term corner candidate with ball skills
29.bio: Johnson is a big corner who excels at the catch point, using his size and leaping ability to challenge receivers and compete for contested throws. The next level will test his consistency as offenses create more difficult matchups and coverage decisions.
29.watch: Control transitions at route breaks and finish tackles after short completions.

30.name: Tye Miller
30.headline: A productive runner with room to broaden his role
30.bio: Miller has produced the most combined rushing yards over the past two seasons, establishing a sustained track record of carrying the ball for his offense. His professional role will grow with dependable execution and the ability to contribute in different situations.
30.watch: Expand his route detail and keep his feet disciplined when the intended lane closes.

31.headline: A starting pathway with another rush answer to develop
31.bio: A four-year player, Smith has never posted huge sack totals but consistently gets to the quarterback and creates disruption beyond the traditional box score. Turning his strengths into a dependable role against stronger competition will be the next challenge.
31.watch: Add a quicker counter and keep his hands accurate when the offensive tackle changes the contact point.
31.name: Hezekiah Smith

32.name: Tyreke Stump
32.headline: A strong safety who can play downhill
32.bio: Stump is a hard-hitting safety who rarely misses tackles and has a reputation for forcing fumbles, bringing reliable physicality to the back of the defense. His transition will depend on sustaining that profile against more polished routes and faster offensive concepts.
32.watch: Read play action patiently and maintain leverage when tackling near the box.

33.name: Kerry Williams Jr.
33.headline: A vertical weapon with a larger route tree to build
33.bio: Williams is a big receiver and vertical threat who can challenge defenses downfield, though his limited route tree will require development as his role expands. His development will be measured by how consistently his strengths translate against faster, more physical coverage.
33.watch: Build strength against press coverage, improve release variety and broaden his route inventory.

34.name: Kemal Sheppard
34.headline: An outside corner with competitive coverage ability
34.bio: Sheppard pairs speed with strong coverage skills, but bigger receivers can challenge him physically and force him to find ways to win through technique. His ability to handle varied assignments against faster offenses will shape his path to playing time.
34.watch: Recognize crossing routes sooner and tackle with consistent leverage.

35.headline: Useful edge pressure with a lighter initial role
35.bio: Lake is an undersized pass rusher with an established package of moves, though adding weight would help him hold up against larger blockers. Turning his strengths into a dependable role against stronger competition will be the next challenge.
35.watch: Improve his run fits and tackling control, then add a dependable answer when the edge closes.
35.name: Desmond Lake

36.headline: An edge rotation piece with room to sharpen the finish
36.bio: A former three-star recruit, Maldanado steadily rose through the ranks and developed a varied collection of pass-rush moves to challenge offensive tackles. His next challenge is translating that profile into consistent impact against stronger, more experienced blockers.
36.watch: Time his separation more effectively and develop a clearer second move after initial contact.
36.name: Ricky Maldanado

37.headline: Useful movement with protection details to sharpen
37.bio: Smith is undersized for an offensive tackle, but his leverage and consistent technique help him hold up and get the job done against larger opponents. His transition will be tested by experienced defenders who can challenge his technique across every snap.
37.watch: Strengthen his anchor and maintain hand position when the rush changes from movement to direct contact.
37.name: Darell Smith

38.headline: Interior disruption with development time on his side
38.bio: A former five-star recruit, Crawford combines an elite athletic profile with solid production, giving him the tools to climb as evaluators study his potential. His development will depend on winning his assignments against experienced blockers in a range of situations.
38.watch: Keep his pad level controlled and avoid losing his run responsibility while searching for an interior opening.
38.name: Bobbie Crawford

39.headline: An interior run defender with a defined early role
39.bio: Francisco brings a classic interior defensive line profile, using his size and run-stopping ability to help control space between the tackles. Turning his strengths into a dependable role against stronger competition will be the next challenge.
39.watch: Separate from blocks more efficiently and develop a more productive passing-down response after first contact.
39.name: Johnathan Francisco

40.name: Amir Robinson
40.headline: A corner with coverage versatility to develop
40.bio: Robinson is a special teams standout who can return punts and kicks, while offering serviceable coverage and a potential role as a second or third corner. His transition will depend on sustaining that profile against more polished routes and faster offensive concepts.
40.watch: Improve route transitions and avoid opening his hips too early.

41.headline: A rotational rusher with a broader role to earn
41.bio: Robinson ranked among college football’s top five in both sacks and combined pressures, winning with production and technique despite a limited athletic profile. The next level will test how consistently his strengths hold up against professional offensive linemen.
41.watch: Hold his edge assignment against the run and connect his initial movement to a more reliable counter.
41.name: Jahmiah Robinson

42.name: Devoreaux Flowers
42.headline: A boundary defender with opportunities on the ball
42.bio: An older small-school prospect, Flowers combines elite athletic tools with several seasons of strong tape, giving scouts an extended track record to evaluate. His ability to handle varied assignments against faster offenses will shape his path to playing time.
42.watch: Finish tackles cleanly and keep his balance through receiver releases.

43.name: De'Quan Coleman
43.headline: A physical rotation back with a clear early role
43.bio: Coleman is a strong runner who welcomes contact and can run through defenders, bringing a physical downhill dimension to the backfield. His ability to handle a varied workload will shape his opportunities at the next level.
43.watch: Improve receiving transitions and lateral resets without losing forward momentum.

44.headline: Useful early snaps, with a more defined ceiling
44.bio: An older tight end with elite catching ability, Morgan-Stewart boasts the best hands in the position group and gives his quarterback a reliable target. His transition will depend on sustaining that value as defenses challenge him with different matchups and responsibilities.
44.watch: Tighten transitions out of breaks and create separation before contested catches become the only answer.
44.name: Tyler Morgan-Stewart

45.headline: A young interior contributor with a stronger rushing-down case
45.bio: Browning is a strong run defender who also carries a set of dependable pass-rush moves, allowing him to win against interior blockers in multiple ways. The next level will test how consistently his strengths hold up against professional offensive linemen.
45.watch: Improve his separation timing and develop a more effective second action when his initial rush is contained.
45.name: Justice Browning

46.headline: A reliable run-game assignment with limited rush impact
46.bio: Schafer can fill gaps and contribute against the run, but must improve as a pass rusher to become a more complete and dependable defensive end. His development will depend on winning his assignments against experienced blockers in a range of situations.
46.watch: Add a more effective counter after first contact while maintaining his dependable run-game positioning.
46.name: Sam Schafer

47.name: Keon Booker
47.headline: A safety with useful range and route awareness
47.bio: The captain of Alabama’s defense, Booker is a reliable tackler who plays close to the line and brings leadership and physicality to the safety position. More complex offensive looks will test how consistently he can execute his responsibilities at the next level.
47.watch: Take cleaner pursuit angles and diagnose route combinations from depth.

48.headline: A workable receiving role with separation still to develop
48.bio: McFarland filled a variety of gaps in Alabama’s offense and produced a high touchdown total, giving his team a versatile option near the end zone. His transition will depend on sustaining that value as defenses challenge him with different matchups and responsibilities.
48.watch: Vary his releases, finish route breaks with conviction and sustain blocks through the end of the play.
48.name: Nik McFarland

49.headline: Interior movement with a starting job still to earn
49.bio: McCue is a powerful run blocker who can overwhelm linebackers and defensive backs in space, though quicker opponents can expose his struggles against speed. His transition will be tested by experienced defenders who can challenge his technique across every snap.
49.watch: Recognize interior exchanges earlier and keep his base controlled when a defender crosses his face.
49.name: Jeramy McCue

50.name: Markus Finn Jr.
50.headline: An outside corner with a developing coverage profile
50.bio: Finn emerged as Missouri’s top defensive back in a strong secondary room, but his ability to process and execute zone coverage remains a key area to improve. His ability to handle varied assignments against faster offenses will shape his path to playing time.
50.watch: Reduce wasted steps out of breaks and recover without drawing contact.

51.name: Keshawn Bell
51.headline: Coverage depth with a path to a larger role
51.bio: An undersized linebacker, Bell offers a hybrid skill set as both a pass-rush specialist and a coverage option, giving a coordinator flexibility in sub-packages. More complex offensive looks will test how consistently he can execute his responsibilities at the next level.
51.watch: Finish open-field tackles and react decisively when routes break underneath.

52.name: Jonathon Aquino
52.headline: An organizer with a measured approach inside
52.bio: Aquino is regarded as the smartest player in the class, processing the game like a chess match and bringing exceptional diagnostic ability to the middle. His transition will depend on sustaining that profile against more polished routes and faster offensive concepts.
52.watch: Separate from climbing blockers while keeping his run fit and coverage landmarks intact.

53.name: James Robinson
53.headline: A physical interior defender built for the run
53.bio: A former five-star recruit, Robinson rose late after finally receiving an opportunity to play, making an immediate impact once he earned meaningful snaps. The next level will test his consistency as offenses create more difficult matchups and coverage decisions.
53.watch: Improve route recognition and change of direction when backs release into space.

54.headline: Contact value with more consistency still to find
54.bio: A former five-star recruit, Bailey has the prototype defensive end build but was buried on the depth chart and saw limited playing time. His development will depend on winning his assignments against experienced blockers in a range of situations.
54.watch: Keep his feet active through contact and improve tackle completion when the ball reaches his edge.
54.name: Kash Bailey

55.headline: Interior movement with a more complete role to develop
55.bio: A late riser with an aggressive, unrestrained style, Andrews has the potential to become a star if he can channel his play with greater control. Turning his strengths into a dependable role against stronger competition will be the next challenge.
55.watch: Improve leverage and contact balance so his interior movement does not come at the expense of his run responsibility.
55.name: Braylen Andrews

56.name: Nick Barrientos
56.headline: The throwing tools are ahead of the consistency
56.bio: A former five-star recruit and Arkansas transfer, Barrientos had a streaky career before finding greater stability on a talented and deep Miami team. His projection will depend on translating those traits into consistent decisions against faster, more complex defenses.
56.watch: Improve short-area touch, repeat his footwork and separate an aggressive opportunity from a forced throw.

57.name: Taylor Smith-Foster
57.headline: A long interior linebacker with downhill presence
57.bio: Smith-Foster brings the size and range to play in the middle of a defense, combining a linebacker’s reach with the ability to cover ground. The next level will test his consistency as offenses create more difficult matchups and coverage decisions.
57.watch: Stay balanced through contact and develop cleaner transitions on passing downs.

58.name: Jack Wilson
58.headline: A run-focused linebacker with a steady pursuit profile
58.bio: Wilson brings elite instincts to the position and helped drive NC State’s defense toward a top ranking through his play and understanding of the game. His ability to handle varied assignments against faster offenses will shape his path to playing time.
58.watch: Read backfield action without overcommitting and improve recovery against routes.

59.name: C.J. Paredes
59.headline: A sturdy edge-of-the-box defender
59.bio: An older linebacker and captain of a strong Miami defense, Paredes brings experience and leadership to a group looking for an established presence. More complex offensive looks will test how consistently he can execute his responsibilities at the next level.
59.watch: Use his hands earlier against blocks and react quicker to releases into the flat.

60.headline: A mobile interior option who needs a firmer base
60.bio: Baines is at his best in a zone blocking scheme, moving his large frame with surprising ease and creating opportunities when the line works laterally. His projection will depend on sustaining that approach against the speed and physicality of professional defensive fronts.
60.watch: Develop a firmer anchor and land his hands more consistently against direct interior pressure.
60.name: Darnell Baines

61.name: Johnny Newman
61.headline: A large receiving target with separation work ahead
61.bio: Newman is a big-bodied receiver whose modest college production leaves his projection tied largely to size, physical potential and the possibility of future development. His development will be measured by how consistently his strengths translate against faster, more physical coverage.
61.watch: Sink into breaks more efficiently and create earlier separation against tight man coverage.

62.headline: A sturdy run contribution with a narrower passing-down role
62.bio: Brothers is a big-bodied defensive end who excels at filling gaps and has the versatility to move inside when a defensive front needs him. His development will depend on winning his assignments against experienced blockers in a range of situations.
62.watch: Separate from blocks sooner and improve the urgency of his first steps on passing downs.
62.name: Jonathan Brothers

63.name: Zac Williams
63.headline: A developmental passer with a narrower margin for error
63.bio: A transfer from Pittsburgh, Williams won the starting job and posted average statistics while showing the physical look of a potential franchise quarterback. His ability to sustain drives against more complex defenses will be central to his professional projection.
63.watch: Clean up routine accuracy, accelerate covered-read decisions and avoid holding the ball into sacks.

64.name: Mike Swizter
64.headline: A deep safety competing for a defined role
64.bio: Swizter excels in zone coverage and brings awareness to the deep field, but his smaller frame can be targeted by opponents in the run game. His transition will depend on sustaining that profile against more polished routes and faster offensive concepts.
64.watch: Improve tackling from depth and react earlier to developing routes.

65.headline: A substantial middle with quicker reactions to develop
65.bio: A redshirt senior, Shea earned recognition as the nation’s best center and brings a polished, experienced presence to the middle of the offensive line. His transition will be tested by experienced defenders who can challenge his technique across every snap.
65.watch: React sooner to quick interior movement and transition cleanly between helping and taking over a defender.
65.name: Matt Shea

66.name: Kevin Rivera
66.headline: A safety prospect with room to refine his angles
66.bio: Rivera is a smart safety who handles the deepest part of the field with ease, using awareness and positioning to protect the defense over the top. His ability to handle varied assignments against faster offenses will shape his path to playing time.
66.watch: Maintain coverage landmarks and take cleaner angles toward the ball.

67.name: Qualeek Leonard
67.headline: Useful size and movement, with a workload to earn
67.bio: A former five-star recruit, Leonard arrives with one strong season of production, giving evaluators a promising peak and a shorter track record to assess. His ability to handle a varied workload will shape his opportunities at the next level.
67.watch: Make quicker interior decisions and improve protection reliability before expanding his workload.

68.name: Nick Matthews
68.headline: A corner who can compete for rotational snaps
68.bio: Matthews is a reliable tackler who generally handles his coverage assignments, although receivers can challenge him over the top when his leverage breaks down. His transition will depend on sustaining that profile against more polished routes and faster offensive concepts.
68.watch: Stay patient against double moves and secure tackles after the catch.

69.name: Terrell Fairbanks
69.headline: A physical rotational prospect with room to grow
69.bio: Fairbanks brings the ability to get after the quarterback and contribute against the run, providing a linebacker profile that can help in multiple situations. The next level will test his consistency as offenses create more difficult matchups and coverage decisions.
69.watch: Recognize blocking schemes earlier and maintain leverage when crossing traffic.

70.headline: A developmental edge with a rush plan to sharpen
70.bio: Nyokare has elite athletic tools but saw limited playing time during his college career, making his projection dependent on developing those traits into consistent production. His development will depend on winning his assignments against experienced blockers in a range of situations.
70.watch: Build a more organized counter plan and improve his ability to finish tackles through contact.
70.name: Kaziri Nyokare

71.headline: A reserve-center pathway with finishing work ahead
71.bio: Bauer is a pass-protecting center whose next step is improving as a run blocker, where more consistent execution would round out his interior profile. His ability to handle different defensive fronts will shape his opportunities at the next level.
71.watch: Sustain control after first contact and improve the consistency of his run-block finish.
71.name: Jacob Bauer

72.headline: A young rush option with a dependable floor to build
72.bio: A former five-star recruit, Thompson flashed as a freshman before his production declined, though his considerable physical tools remain central to his projection. His next challenge is translating that profile into consistent impact against stronger, more experienced blockers.
72.watch: Coordinate his hands with his first steps and improve run positioning before expanding his workload.
72.name: Shad Thompson

73.headline: A tall tackle with a substantial technique assignment
73.bio: Wilkins is a small-school standout with the traits and skills to compete in the NFL, bringing an encouraging foundation into a higher level of competition. His transition will be tested by experienced defenders who can challenge his technique across every snap.
73.watch: Improve set angles, lower his pad level and recover without reaching after losing position.
73.name: Jaden Wilkins

74.headline: Downfield options to develop, routine details to fix
74.bio: One of two LSU tight ends in the class, Jackson is a vertical threat with soft hands who can stretch coverage and finish catches downfield. How reliably he handles varied assignments will determine the size of his role at the next level.
74.watch: Improve ball tracking and release timing, then broaden the routes he can execute reliably.
74.name: Theodore Jackson Jr.

75.headline: A passing-down opportunity that still needs a finish
75.bio: A former linebacker, Jennings is undersized for a defensive end but brings exceptional speed and has shown he can compete effectively along the line. Turning his strengths into a dependable role against stronger competition will be the next challenge.
75.watch: Improve contact balance and develop a reliable second action when his first rush path is closed.
75.name: Jaquann Jennings

76.headline: Rushing value with protection that needs to catch up
76.bio: A three-year starter, Davison produced his best season in year two and brings extensive starting experience to his evaluation at right tackle. His projection will depend on sustaining that approach against the speed and physicality of professional defensive fronts.
76.watch: Improve set discipline against the edge and stay connected when a defender avoids his initial contact.
76.name: Dee Davison

77.headline: A rotational guard with interior pressure to clean up
77.bio: A former four-star recruit and Colorado transfer, Lee developed later in his career and emerged as a more intriguing guard prospect after that late bloom. His transition will be tested by experienced defenders who can challenge his technique across every snap.
77.watch: Identify interior exchanges sooner and keep his feet and hands coordinated when the front shifts.
77.name: Brandon Lee

78.name: Brantley Smith
78.headline: A developmental inside linebacker with useful size
78.bio: Smith is a big middle linebacker who compensates for limited athleticism with a high football IQ and an understanding of how plays develop. His ability to handle varied assignments against faster offenses will shape his path to playing time.
78.watch: Reduce missed tackles and maintain leverage when pursuing across the formation.

79.headline: Movement potential with a dependable floor still to build
79.bio: Fisher is a run-blocking tackle who excels at getting upfield to deliver lead blocks, using his movement to create room beyond the line of scrimmage. His ability to handle different defensive fronts will shape his opportunities at the next level.
79.watch: Improve first-contact accuracy, keep recovery steps controlled and sustain blocks beyond initial positioning.
79.name: Colt Fisher

80.headline: Interior depth with a defined rushing-down assignment
80.bio: Vanwinkle was a bright spot on a struggling USC defense, standing out as a reliable run stopper who could anchor his area of the front. His next challenge is translating that profile into consistent impact against stronger, more experienced blockers.
80.watch: Keep his pad level controlled and develop a quicker way to separate once the blocker establishes contact.
80.name: Hugh Vanwinkle

81.name: Isaac Almonte
81.headline: A developmental corner with ball skills to build on
81.bio: Almonte is an effective smaller corner with good athletic ability and tools, finding ways to compete in coverage despite giving up size to some receivers. The next level will test his consistency as offenses create more difficult matchups and coverage decisions.
81.watch: Close underneath space earlier and improve tackling through contact.

82.name: Rocco Weatherly
82.headline: A strong safety who can help near the line
82.bio: Weatherly is a big-bodied safety with the physical traits to dominate, but his inconsistent tape leaves a wide range of outcomes in his projection. His ability to handle varied assignments against faster offenses will shape his path to playing time.
82.watch: Keep his coverage landmarks while continuing to finish in run support.

83.name: Demond Henderson
83.headline: A rotational option who needs cleaner possessions
83.bio: Henderson has elite physical traits despite modest college statistics, making his evaluation a bet on what those tools could become with further development. His ability to handle a varied workload will shape his opportunities at the next level.
83.watch: Protect the ball through contact, eliminate hesitation and earn trust on passing downs.

84.headline: A blocking role to earn before the target count grows
84.bio: Cook is a blocking tight end with dependable possession skills, offering particular value in heavier offensive packages and formations featuring three tight ends. His transition will depend on sustaining that value as defenses challenge him with different matchups and responsibilities.
84.watch: Develop cleaner releases and reliable short catches while maintaining his blocking contribution.
84.name: Daronte Cook

85.name: Jaden Millhouse
85.headline: A developmental corner with a competitive foundation
85.bio: Millhouse is a tall, thin corner who covers well, but must bring more physicality against the run to hold up when opponents target his side. The next level will test his consistency as offenses create more difficult matchups and coverage decisions.
85.watch: Improve tackling consistency and hold leverage through the full route.

86.name: Jaylon Clarke
86.headline: Downfield size that still needs a dependable floor
86.bio: A former five-star recruit and Michigan transfer, Clarke specializes in contested jump balls and gives an offense a target who can compete above defenders. His ability to earn targets against experienced corners will determine the size of his early role.
86.watch: Improve ball tracking, tighten release timing and become useful on nonvertical routes.

87.name: Mike Scheidegger
87.headline: A depth candidate who can organize the front
87.bio: A small-school standout, Scheidegger is a sure tackler with a middling athletic profile, giving him a clear defensive foundation as he moves up in competition. More complex offensive looks will test how consistently he can execute his responsibilities at the next level.
87.watch: Speed up his first read and work free from blockers without losing gap integrity.

88.name: Sammie Bonilla
88.headline: A compact linebacker competing for rotational work
88.bio: Bonilla is a smaller run-focused linebacker who attacks contact and delivers big hits, bringing a physical presence despite his shorter stature. His transition will depend on sustaining that profile against more polished routes and faster offensive concepts.
88.watch: Finish tackles more consistently and stay patient when receivers cross his zone.

89.name: Joseph Lomeli
89.headline: An underneath contributor with a limited initial projection
89.bio: Lomeli put up strong college receiving statistics despite a limited athletic profile, making his evaluation a contrast between proven production and physical upside. His development will be measured by how consistently his strengths translate against faster, more physical coverage.
89.watch: Generate separation against man coverage and add more value after short receptions.

90.name: T.J. Chausiku
90.headline: A strong safety with rotational potential
90.bio: At 6-foot-4, Chausiku offers rare safety size and excellent ball skills, though his thinner frame leaves room to grow as a potential third-round steal. His ability to handle varied assignments against faster offenses will shape his path to playing time.
90.watch: Stay under control when triggering downhill and improve open-field tackling.

91.name: Tazwel Mason
91.headline: A developmental safety with coverage work ahead
91.bio: A small-school safety, Mason put up numbers that compare favorably with the class’s top defensive backs, earning attention through his production on the field. More complex offensive looks will test how consistently he can execute his responsibilities at the next level.
91.watch: Improve tackling angles and maintain spacing against layered routes.

92.name: Kiaan Brown
92.headline: Receiving value in a role that still needs definition
92.bio: Brown is a former wide receiver recruit who brings receiving ability to the backfield, giving an offense a natural pass-catching option at running back. His transition will hinge on creating efficient gains and contributing consistently across different offensive situations.
92.watch: Improve protection, win routes beyond easy outlets and build evidence for a larger rushing role.

93.headline: A developmental guard with an anchor to strengthen
93.bio: Varela is an undersized guard who excels in pass protection and moves well for his size, offering an athletic interior option for a passing offense. His transition will be tested by experienced defenders who can challenge his technique across every snap.
93.watch: Strengthen his anchor, improve strike timing and reduce penalties before taking on a larger workload.
93.name: Renaldo Varela

94.headline: A developmental receiving option with trust to build
94.bio: A Minnesota transfer, Whitney produced solid receiving yardage but few touchdowns, giving evaluators useful evidence of production outside the end zone. How reliably he handles varied assignments will determine the size of his role at the next level.
94.watch: Improve catch-point adjustments, sharpen route pacing and become dependable on routine underneath throws.
94.name: Brendan Whitney

95.headline: Reserve-edge competition with more impact to prove
95.bio: A former walk-on and captain of a talented Michigan team, Whitt rose through the program despite a limited athletic tool set. Turning his strengths into a dependable role against stronger competition will be the next challenge.
95.watch: Improve tackling through contact and separate from blocks more efficiently before seeking a larger role.
95.name: Denver Whitt

96.headline: A developmental edge who needs a more complete sequence
96.bio: A team captain, McKinley produced strong numbers on an otherwise struggling Illinois defense, standing out as a productive presence on the edge. His next challenge is translating that profile into consistent impact against stronger, more experienced blockers.
96.watch: Connect his first contact to a useful counter and improve his control when finishing at the edge.
96.name: Jerrick McKinley
